title: The House Without Questions — Public Notice
location: General Access Terminal — The House Without Questions, Lower City
author: The House Without Questions
content:
IF YOU HAVE NOWHERE ELSE TO GO.

Come to the House. We will take you in. We will clothe you, feed you, and protect you. We will ask you nothing.

If you have something you need done, come to the House. Tell us what it is. If it can be done, we will tell you what it costs. If you pay, it will be done. We will ask you nothing about why.

We have been here longer than this city. We have been here longer than most things on this world.

We do not advertise what we have accomplished. We do not keep records that anyone else can read. We do not confirm or deny any specific task on our behalf. We do not discuss our history, our methods, or our current engagements.

What we will tell you: we have never failed to accomplish a task that was within the bounds of the possible. We have occasionally had to redefine what 'possible' means, but we have not failed.

We do not accept tasks that require us to harm those who have previously sheltered with us. This is the only restriction.

Everything else is a matter of price.

—

[Handwritten at the bottom, clearly not official:]

I sheltered here once. Three years ago. They didn't ask me anything. I stayed for nine days and they fed me and no one touched me and when I left they didn't ask me where I was going.

I don't know what they are. I don't know how old. I know they were here before the Brotherhood and before His Grace and before the gangs.

I know they are still here.

That's worth something.

title: Blood Pit — Tonight's Card
location: General Access Terminal — Blood Pit Arena, Lower City
author: Blood Pit Management
content:
BLOOD PIT — TONIGHT'S CARD

Doors open at half-cycle. Bets accepted until the second bell.

Event 1: Melee bracket, four contestants. Three volunteers, one not. Standard rules (none).

Event 2: Alien predator exhibition. Species: Undisclosed. Origin: Foreven Sector, recovered from a derelict. Handler advises spectators in the first three rows to sign the disclaimer. — Related recovery detail: [[connect: scrapheap]]

Event 3: Steel cage. Two contestants. Both volunteers. Personal grievance match — details posted at the betting desk.

Event 4: The main event. Gladiator versus robot. The robot has been modified. Our technician says it is now operating outside its original design parameters and he is not entirely comfortable with what it has started to do between events. We consider this excellent atmosphere.

—

Special notice: A private booth has been reserved for this evening by a party who paid double for guaranteed privacy. We note this only because it is unusual enough to mention to the management log. All other guests: standard seating.

—

Note from the management: If you see something in the lower pens that you cannot identify, do not attempt to interact with it. We are still determining where it came from and whether it is ours.

title: Blood Pit — Historical Bout Record
location: General Access Terminal — Blood Pit Arena, Lower City
author: Blood Pit Management — Historical Archive
content:
HISTORICAL BOUT RECORD — SELECTED HIGHLIGHTS

Year 1094: The bout known as 'The Wildeman Affair.' A Vargr combatant — unregistered, entered under the alias 'Mad Dog' — defeated three consecutive opponents including a modified security drone and a K'Kree sharpshooter on a bet. Left before we could offer a contract. Still have the name on file if he ever comes back.

Year 1096: Exhibition match, alien specimen versus three armed volunteers. Specimen was described on intake as 'petrified, probably inert.' It was not inert. Volunteers did not survive. Specimen was eventually subdued. We do not discuss the method. We have a strict policy now about intake classification.

Year 1098: The last time anyone brought in a specimen from that Foreven derelict sale. We are not accepting further stock from that particular source.

Year 1101: Corporate-sponsored grudge match. Sponsors wished to remain anonymous. Combatant lost. The sponsors were less interested in the fight than in testing something they had fitted to the combatant. What they were testing was not disclosed to us. We are noting this retroactively because we found a piece of equipment in the pit afterward that none of our staff recognized.

[The last line of the file has been partially overwritten with a single phrase, author unknown:]

'The stone was not the only one.'

BIOLOGICAL INTAKE RECORD — EVENT 2 SPECIMEN

Specimen designation: LOT-2-0212
Origin: Foreven Sector. Recovered from a derelict by a GeDeCo-affiliated salvage contractor.
Acquired via: Third-party broker, Cliff District. Brokered six days ago. Delivery: three days ago.

Biological classification (filed):
— Initial assessment: INERT. Petrified. No vital signs. Recommended as display specimen only.
— Revised (Day 210, 0200): BIOLOGICAL — DORMANT. Signs of metabolic activity at very low level. Recommend do not handle without containment.
— Revised (Day 210, 1100): BIOLOGICAL — ACTIVE. Specimen responded to lighting change. Containment is holding. Handler advises: 'It is waiting for something.'
— Current classification: RECLASSIFY PENDING.

Physical description: Folded. Limb count indeterminate. Approximately 1.4 meters across. The surface texture has changed since intake — it was uniform on arrival and is now showing differentiated regions that were not present. The handler believes this is 'waking up.'

Handler advisory note: 'I have handled alien specimens for twelve years. I have never had one that made the other specimens in the adjacent cages go quiet. They have been quiet since this one arrived. I do not consider this a good sign.'

Management response to handler advisory: 'The crowd will love it.'

content:
NOTE FROM HOUSE ADMINISTRATION:

This fragment was found behind a sealed wall panel during renovation fourteen years ago. We have not been able to date it using any technique available to us. The language is a variant of early Vilani Trade Pidgin, but with grammatical structures we cannot place in any known period.

We are filing it because we believe in documentation.

—

[LEGIBLE SECTION — TRANSLATION APPROXIMATE:]

'A place is needed where those who have nothing may rest, and where questions are not a tool of the powerful.'

'This place is not new. It has been in many locations. The location changes. The purpose does not.'

'Those who keep this place are not its owners. They are its current carriers. The place will outlast them as it has outlasted those before.'

'There is a mark. Those who know it will find us. Those who do not know it will find us anyway, because the ones who need a house without questions always find their way to one.'

—

[ILLEGIBLE SECTION]

—

[FINAL LEGIBLE LINE:]

'The first time this house was kept, the stars were not yet in this arrangement. We note this for context, not as evidence of anything supernatural. We are practical people. We simply keep records.'

—

Note from current administration: We have been here for eleven years. We do not know how long the house before us was here. We know that the wall panel was sealed at least one hundred and forty years ago based on the construction method. We know the text is older than that.

We keep records.
